pck: Negative numbers represent quantities opposite to a chosen reference or direction, such as temperatures below zero, westward travel, or expenses.
Positive numbers are greater than zero; negative numbers are less than zero; zero is neither positive nor negative.
Integers include positive integers, zero, and negative integers; fractions may also be positive or negative.
A rational number is any number expressible as a ratio of two integers with a nonzero denominator.
A set is a collection of objects; examples include the set of rational numbers, integers, negative numbers, and nonnegative integers.
A number line is a line with a chosen origin, direction, and unit length used to represent numbers as points.
On a number line, positive numbers lie to the right of the origin and negative numbers to the left; a number's distance from the origin gives its absolute value.
On a number line, numbers farther to the right are greater; every positive number is greater than zero, and every negative number is less than zero.
The opposite of a number has the same absolute value and the opposite sign; the only number equal to its own opposite is zero.
Opposite numbers are represented by points equally distant from the origin on opposite sides of the number line.
The opposite of zero is zero.
A minus sign before a number indicates its opposite; a plus sign before a number indicates the number itself.
The absolute value of a number is its distance from zero on the number line, written |a|.
A positive number's absolute value is itself, zero's absolute value is zero, and a negative number's absolute value is its opposite.
The absolute value of every rational number is nonnegative: |a| >= 0.
For two negative numbers, the number with the smaller absolute value is greater.
To add rational numbers with the same sign, add their absolute values and keep the common sign.
To add rational numbers with different signs, subtract the smaller absolute value from the larger and use the sign of the number with the larger absolute value; opposite numbers sum to zero.
Adding zero to a number leaves the number unchanged.
Rational addition satisfies the commutative and associative laws: a + b = b + a and (a + b) + c = a + (b + c).
Rational addition can model practical situations such as changes in position, temperature, or total weight.
The opposite of a number is the additive inverse that sums with it to zero.
The associative and commutative laws can simplify sums of several rational numbers by regrouping or reordering terms.
Subtracting a rational number is equivalent to adding its opposite: a - b = a + (-b).
Converting subtraction to addition makes rational subtraction follow the familiar addition rules.
Rational subtraction can model differences such as changes in altitude or temperature.
A sum or difference expression can be rewritten using addition alone by replacing each subtraction with addition of the opposite.
After rewriting a mixed sum and difference as addition, terms may be regrouped and reordered using the commutative and associative laws.
The Nine Chapters on the Mathematical Art is an ancient Chinese mathematical text that includes early methods for working with positive and negative quantities.
Its chapter on equations describes operations with positive and negative quantities in solving practical problems.
The ancient rule for adding and subtracting positive and negative quantities corresponds to modern signed-number arithmetic.
Modern explanations of signed numbers build on the idea that positive and negative quantities represent opposite directions or effects.
Historically, the use of negative numbers developed at different times across mathematical traditions; Chinese mathematical texts discussed them centuries before their widespread adoption in Europe.

For rational multiplication, multiply the absolute values; the product is positive when the factors have the same sign and negative when they have different signs. Any product with a zero factor is zero.
Rational multiplication is commutative and associative: ab = ba and (ab)c = a(bc).
The commutative and associative laws can simplify products, for example (-10) × (1/3) × 0.1 × 6 = -2.
For a product of nonzero rational numbers, the sign is positive when the number of negative factors is even and negative when it is odd; multiply absolute values to find the magnitude.
A product with a zero factor is zero.
Rational multiplication satisfies the distributive law: a(b + c) = ab + ac.
Division by a nonzero rational number can be converted to multiplication by its reciprocal: a ÷ b = a × (1/b).
Two nonzero numbers are reciprocals if their product is 1; the reciprocal of a/b is b/a.
To divide rational numbers, divide their absolute values and use the sign rule for multiplication. Division by zero is undefined.
Every rational number can be expressed as a ratio of two integers with a nonzero denominator.
A power represents repeated multiplication of the same factor; the result is called the power.
In a^n, a is the base and n is the exponent.
A product of nonzero factors is positive when the number of negative factors is even and negative when it is odd.
Scientific notation writes a number as a × 10^n, where 1 ≤ |a| < 10 and n is an integer.
Evaluate rational-number expressions by following the order of operations: parentheses, exponents, multiplication and division from left to right, then addition and subtraction from left to right.
Addition and subtraction are first-level operations, multiplication and division are second-level operations, and exponents are third-level operations.
To divide fractions, multiply by the reciprocal of the divisor.
Efficient rational arithmetic depends on following the order of operations and choosing useful regrouping or equivalent forms.
An approximate value is close to an exact value and is useful when exact results are unnecessary or difficult to obtain.
The stated precision of an approximate value identifies the place value to which it has been rounded.
Rounding is a common way to obtain approximate values; select the precision appropriate to the task.
Calculators can perform complex arithmetic efficiently and support practical problem solving.
A calculator evaluates an expression entered through its keys or interface.
Rational numbers are numbers that can be expressed as ratios of integers with nonzero denominators.
A number line represents numbers as points relative to an origin, direction, and unit length.
Opposite numbers have the same absolute value and opposite signs; absolute value is distance from zero.
A repeating decimal can be expressed as a fraction by setting it equal to a variable and solving the resulting equation.
Introducing negative numbers extends the number system and makes subtraction possible for any pair of rational numbers.
Rewriting a problem in a simpler equivalent form is a useful mathematical strategy.
Rational arithmetic follows the commutative, associative, and distributive laws where applicable.
